sentences.en: SHANKAR VEDANTAM, From NPR, this is HIDDEN BRAIN.
sentences.zh: Shankar Vedantam，来自NPR，这里是《Hidden Brain》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam. Today, we have a story that will change the way you think about many things - poverty, loneliness, time, even hunger.
sentences.zh: 我是 Shankar Vedantam。今天，我们有一个故事，它将改变你对许多事物的看法——贫穷、孤独、时间，甚至是饥饿。

sentences.en: It's a tale about the psychological phenomenon of scarcity.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于稀缺心理现象的故事。

sentences.en: It affects nearly everything in our lives and connects people who appear to have nothing in common.
sentences.zh: 它几乎影响着我们生活中的方方面面，并将那些看似毫无共同点的人们联系在一起。

sentences.en: The story of scarcity is a story of how not having enough of what you need can become the only thing that matters to you.
sentences.zh: 关于稀缺的故事，讲述了当你缺乏所需之物时，这种匮乏如何变成对你而言唯一重要的事情。

sentences.en: That, I think, is the basic scarcity instinct.
sentences.zh: 我想，这就是最基本的稀缺本能。

sentences.en: We're hungry. And then this thing starts going off in the head saying, do you realize we're hungry?
sentences.zh: 我们饿了。然后大脑里就开始有个声音在说：“你意识到我们饿了吗？”

sentences.en: Have I mentioned we're hungry? We're hungry.
sentences.zh: 我提过我们饿了吗？我们饿了。

sentences.en: This week on HIDDEN BRAIN... Think deeply.
sentences.zh: 本周在《Hidden Brain》……深度思考。

sentences.en: VEDANTAM:...We continue our annual summer series, You 2.0...
sentences.zh: Vedantam：……我们继续我们的年度夏季系列节目“You 2.0”……

sentences.en: Authenticity is contagious. (Laughter) I have been dragged into this all the way kicking and screaming.
sentences.zh: 真实具有传染性。（笑声）我是一直被连拖带拽地拉进来的，又踢又叫。

sentences.en: VEDANTAM:...Ideas and advice about how you can respond to life's chaos...
sentences.zh: Vedantam：……关于你如何应对生活混乱的理念和建议……

sentences.en: Let me just do a - just check to my inbox...
sentences.zh: 让我做个——检查一下我的收件箱……

sentences.en: Just check... Just check... Just check to my phone real quick.
sentences.zh: 就查一下……就查一下……赶快查一下我的手机。

sentences.en: VEDANTAM:...With wisdom.
sentences.zh: Vedantam：……带着智慧。

sentences.en: This week - how we get in - and out - of the scarcity trap.
sentences.zh: 本周——我们如何陷入——以及摆脱——稀缺陷阱。

sentences.en: My name is Brandy Drew (ph). I'm from Detroit, Mich.
sentences.zh: 我叫 Brandy Drew。我来自密歇根州底特律。

sentences.en: Brandy Drew has a story that may sound familiar to you, a story of poverty and debt.
sentences.zh: Brandy Drew 有一个对你来说可能并不陌生的故事，一个关于贫穷和债务的故事。

sentences.en: It's the kind of story that may lead people to quick conclusions, so pay attention to your own.
sentences.zh: 这是一种容易让人迅速下结论的故事，所以请注意你自己的判断。

sentences.en: Brandy is now 37. Six years ago, her life unraveled.
sentences.zh: Brandy 现在 37 岁。六年前，她的生活分崩离析。

sentences.en: At the time, she ran the dining services department at a senior living facility.
sentences.zh: 当时，她在一家高级生活护理中心管理餐饮服务部门。

sentences.en: She'd been with the company that ran it for more than a decade.
sentences.zh: 她在那家运营公司工作了十多年。

sentences.en: One day, she made a mistake. I was just in a rush to get home.
sentences.zh: 有一天，她犯了一个错误。我当时只是急着回家。

sentences.en: That was all - because day care closes at 6.
sentences.zh: 就这么简单——因为日托中心6点关门。

sentences.en: I get off at 5. It was, like, maybe a 10-mile drive, busy traffic area.
sentences.zh: 我5点下班。大概有10英里的车程，交通非常拥挤。

sentences.en: And I knew I had to pick up diapers, and the easiest thing for me I thought would be to pick them up before I picked the baby up.
sentences.zh: 我知道我得去买尿布，我想对我来说最简单的事情就是在去接宝宝之前把尿布买好。

sentences.en: So Brandy stopped at a store, ran in and grabbed the diapers.
sentences.zh: 于是 Brandy 在一家商店停了下来，跑进去拿了尿布。

sentences.en: She swiped her credit card at the self-checkout station and raced out.
sentences.zh: 她在自助结账机上刷了信用卡，然后冲了出去。

sentences.en: It turns out, she used the wrong card - not her own but the company credit card.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，她用错了卡——用的不是她自己的卡，而是公司的信用卡。

sentences.en: But what's crazy is I didn't realize at that moment.
sentences.zh: 但疯狂的是，我当时根本没意识到。

sentences.en: I didn't realize until my supervisor called me in and said, hey, what's this purchase?
sentences.zh: 直到我的主管把我叫过去说，嘿，这是什么消费？

sentences.en: So had she not said anything, I don't think I would have realized that.
sentences.zh: 所以如果她什么都没说，我想我是不会意识到的。

sentences.en: Brandy carried the card in case she needed to buy dining supplies for work.
sentences.zh: Brandy 随身带着这张卡，以防她需要为工作购买餐饮用品。

sentences.en: She'd never had a problem before, never been reprimanded.
sentences.zh: 她以前从来没有出过问题，也从未受到过训斥。

sentences.en: She thought an apology and an explanation would do.
sentences.zh: 她以为一个道歉和一个解释就能解决问题。

sentences.en: And her response was, well, you know we have to terminate you.
sentences.zh: 而她的回复是，嗯，你知道我们不得不解雇你。

sentences.en: And I'm like, no, I didn't know that. Like, can I just pay you back?
sentences.zh: 我说，不，我不知道。我是说，我可以直接还钱吗？

sentences.en: It was only - what? - 12 bucks. And she said, no, in cases like that, you automatically have to terminate the employee.
sentences.zh: 才——多少？——12块钱。她说，不，遇到这种情况，你必须自动被解雇。

sentences.en: I just cried. I cried for, like, a whole day because I couldn't believe it.
sentences.zh: 我只是哭。我哭了一整天，因为我简直不敢相信。

sentences.en: I didn't want to go home and tell my kids what had happened.
sentences.zh: 我不想回家告诉孩子们发生了什么。

sentences.en: I didn't want to tell my husband what had happened.
sentences.zh: 我不想告诉丈夫发生了什么。

sentences.en: I just didn't know what to do at that point.
sentences.zh: 那一刻我真的不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: I felt like - I felt like a failure as a parent because I didn't provide a good example, even though it was a mistake.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己——我觉得自己作为一个父母很失败，因为我没有树立好榜样，尽管这只是个失误。

sentences.en: Brandy earned more than her husband, so the loss of the job hit hard.
sentences.zh: Brandy 的收入比丈夫高，因此失去工作对她的打击沉重。

sentences.en: She felt like a loser. She tried to bring in money doing odd jobs, like cooking takeaway meals, but the stress grew.
sentences.zh: 她觉得自己是个失败者。她试图通过做零工来赚钱，比如做外卖餐食，但压力越来越大。

sentences.en: Brandy and her husband began fighting. She had supported him when he'd been laid off a few years earlier, and she'd expected he'd do the same for her.
sentences.zh: Brandy 和她的丈夫开始争吵。几年前他被裁员时她曾支持过他，她本指望他现在也能这样对她。

sentences.en: But he felt a layoff was different. He was mad that she'd made a stupid mistake.
sentences.zh: 但他觉得裁员情况不同。他很生气她犯了这么蠢的错误。

sentences.en: The final argument was that I left out the house that morning.
sentences.zh: 最后的争吵发生在那天早晨我出门的时候。

sentences.en: I was going to job interviews. I had two interviews that day.
sentences.zh: 我正要去参加面试。那天我有两场面试。

sentences.en: And I didn't purchase toilet paper. So when he got home from work that day, there was no toilet paper.
sentences.zh: 而我没有买卫生纸。所以当他那天晚上下班回家时，没有卫生纸。

sentences.en: When I came in with the kids, he just immediately started yelling, you can't keep yourself together.
sentences.zh: 我和孩子们一进门，他就立刻开始大吼大叫，你连自己都管不好。

sentences.en: You can't do this. You can't do that. So I walked right back out the door, and I never looked back.
sentences.zh: 你什么都做不好。你连这个也做不好。所以我马上转身夺门而出，头也没回。

sentences.en: Without steady employment and a husband to help with bills, Brandy watched anxiously as her household supplies dwindled.
sentences.zh: 没有了稳定的工作和帮她分担账单的丈夫，Brandy 焦虑地看着家里的物资一天天减少。

sentences.en: She worried constantly about money.
sentences.zh: 她整天为钱的事发愁。

sentences.en: To make ends meet, she ordered a new credit card.
sentences.zh: 为了勉强维持生计，她申请了一张新信用卡。

sentences.en: The day it arrived, Brandy tore open the envelope.
sentences.zh: 卡到的那天，Brandy 撕开信封。

sentences.en: She grabbed the card and ran out the door.
sentences.zh: 她抓起卡冲出了家门。

sentences.en: I went straight to Walmart and I bought, like, a family size of toilet paper, family size of laundry detergent.
sentences.zh: 我直接去了沃尔玛，买了一大包家庭装的卫生纸，家庭装的洗衣液。

sentences.en: Like, I stocked up on things all at once whether than keeping it handy just in case.
sentences.zh: 就像是一次性把东西囤够，而不是以防万一随用随买。

sentences.en: So I, like, maxed it out within the first couple of days that I had it rather than holding on to it for emergency purposes.
sentences.zh: 所以，我在拿到卡的头几天就把额度刷爆了，而不是把它留作紧急备用。

sentences.en: And in that moment, as she was maxing out the credit card on the household supplies she needed, Brandy forgot about things that were slightly less pressing.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，当她刷爆信用卡购买她需要的日用品时，Brandy 忘掉了那些稍微不那么紧迫的事情。

sentences.en: What I didn't think about is, what about gas money?
sentences.zh: 我当时没有考虑到的是，汽油钱怎么办？

sentences.en: I didn't consider what gas would cost. That was, like, the biggest thing.
sentences.zh: 我没考虑油费要多少。那可以说是最大的一笔开销。

sentences.en: It was always hard to have gas. And, of course, there was the credit card bill itself.
sentences.zh: 买汽油总是很艰难。当然，还有信用卡账单本身。

sentences.en: The first two months, I paid the minimum payment.
sentences.zh: 前两个月，我只还了最低还款额。

sentences.en: And then I just stopped paying because I couldn't afford to pay.
sentences.zh: 然后我就索性不还了，因为根本付不起。

sentences.en: I didn't pay that card off until I got my tax refund the following year.
sentences.zh: 直到第二年拿到退税，我才把那张卡还清。

sentences.en: By the time I paid it off, it was over $800 for a $500 card.
sentences.zh: 等我还清的时候，一张500美元额度的卡已经欠了800多美元。

sentences.en: More and more, Brandy felt trapped by debt.
sentences.zh: Brandy 越来越觉得自己被债务困住了。

sentences.en: She no longer had options. It came down to, pay the bills or feed the kids.
sentences.zh: 她已经别无选择。归根结底，要么付账单，要么给孩子买吃的。

sentences.en: It's just overwhelming trying to juggle all of those things and still maintain a certain state of mind so that my children wouldn't see me struggle.
sentences.zh: 试着兼顾所有这一切，还要保持一定的精神状态以免孩子们看到我的挣扎，这实在让人不堪重负。

sentences.en: In retrospect, Brandy can see the mistakes she made.
sentences.zh: 回想起来，Brandy 能够看到自己犯下的错误。

sentences.en: If she had made a budget for the whole month, she might have remembered she needed to account for gas.
sentences.zh: 如果她做了一个整月的预算，她可能就会记起她需要把油费算进去。

sentences.en: If she had focused on the big picture, she might not have maxed out a credit card she couldn't afford to pay back.
sentences.zh: 如果她把目光放长远，她可能就不会刷爆一张她根本还不起的信用卡了。

sentences.en: Why did Brandy make these mistakes? It's easy to say she was being irresponsible.
sentences.zh: 为什么 Brandy 会犯这些错误？人们很容易说她不负责任。

sentences.en: But here's the thing. She had always been careful and conscientious.
sentences.zh: 但关键在于：她一直以来都是个小心谨慎、认真负责的人。

sentences.en: Did something cause her to behave differently?
sentences.zh: 是什么导致她的行为发生了变化？

sentences.en: When you have scarcity and it creates a scarcity mindset, it leads you to take certain behaviors which, in the short term, help you manage scarcity but in the long term only make matters worse.
sentences.zh: 当你陷入稀缺并因此产生一种稀缺心态时，它会促使你采取某些行为：这些行为在短期内能帮应对稀缺，但在长期来看只会让情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: When we come back, how the scarcity trap changes the way we think.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们将探讨稀缺陷阱是如何改变我们的思维方式的。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续关注。

sentences.en: After she lost her job, Brandy fell deeper and deeper into debt.
sentences.zh: 失业后，Brandy 越陷越深，债务越积越多。

sentences.en: One big reason is that she made a series of decisions that improved her life in the moment but made it worse in the long run.
sentences.zh: 一个主要原因在于，她做了一系列在当下能改善生活、但从长远来看却让生活变得更糟的决定。

sentences.en: She could have used the new credit card only for emergencies, but instead, she maxed it out in a couple of days.
sentences.zh: 她本可以把新信用卡留作紧急情况下使用，但她却在几天之内把它刷爆了。

sentences.en: To understand why she did this, I want to take you to a completely different time and place because it reveals something important about Brandy's story.
sentences.zh: 为了解她为什么要这么做，我想带大家回到一个完全不同的时代和地方，因为它揭示了 Brandy 故事中重要的一面。

sentences.en: It's 1944. World War II is nearing its end.
sentences.zh: 那是 1944 年。第二次世界大战接近尾声。

sentences.en: Europe is on the verge of mass famine. Aid workers desperately need guidance on how to bring people back from the brink of starvation.
sentences.zh: 欧洲正处于大规模饥荒的边缘。救援人员迫切需要指导，以了解如何将人们从饥饿的边缘拯救回来。

sentences.en: Researchers at the University of Minnesota thought they could help.
sentences.zh: 明尼苏达大学的研究人员认为他们可以帮上忙。

sentences.en: They launched a year-long experiment. As a 2002 documentary made by the university explains, the volunteers were conscientious objectors who still wanted to serve their country.
sentences.zh: 他们发起了一项为期一年的实验。正如该大学 2002 年制作的一部纪录片所解释的那样，志愿者们都是 conscientious objectors（兵役拒服者），但他们仍然想为国家效力。

sentences.en: The experiment - the volunteers had to go on a starvation diet.
sentences.zh: 这项实验要求志愿者们遵循饥饿饮食法。

sentences.en: Thirty-six young men, most of them Quakers, Mennonites or Church of Brethren members, moved into the south tower of the Memorial Stadium, which would be their home for a year.
sentences.zh: 三十六名年轻男子，大多是贵格会、门诺会或弟兄会成员，搬进了纪念体育场的南塔，那里将是他们一年的家。

sentences.en: Many took courses at the university, even as they grew thinner and thinner.
sentences.zh: 许多人在大学里选修课程，尽管他们日渐消瘦。

sentences.en: The young men became walking scarecrows.
sentences.zh: 这些年轻男子变成了行走的稻草人。

sentences.en: Some grew so weak and bony, they couldn't sit without cushions or raise their arms to wash their hair.
sentences.zh: 有些人虚弱骨感得甚至无法在没有坐垫的情况下安坐，也无法抬起胳膊洗头。

sentences.en: I remember being a little bit critical of guys in the early part who would lick their plates.
sentences.zh: 我还记得早期对那些舔盘子的家伙有点评头论足。

sentences.en: I thought that was really pretty crude. Henry Scholberg was one of the volunteers.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那真的非常粗鲁。Henry Scholberg 是志愿者之一。

sentences.en: He recalled the experience in the documentary.
sentences.zh: 他在纪录片中回忆了这段经历。

sentences.en: By the time we were into about the second month of it, I was doing it myself.
sentences.zh: 大约到了第二个月的时候，我自己也开始这么做了。

sentences.en: You just needed every single calorie you could get your hands on.
sentences.zh: 你简直需要你能弄到的每一卡路里热量。

sentences.en: The results of the starvation experiment were eventually published and remain an important academic reference on nutrition, famine and eating disorders.
sentences.zh: 这项饥饿实验的结果最终得以发表，并至今仍是营养学、饥荒和进食障碍领域重要的学术参考资料。

sentences.en: But recently, two researchers became intrigued with the 70-year-old study for a completely different reason.
sentences.zh: 但最近，两位研究人员对这项已有 70 年历史的研究产生了浓厚的兴趣，原因完全不同。

sentences.en: They were interested in what the lack of food did not to the body but to the mind.
sentences.zh: 他们感兴趣的是，食物匮乏对身体没有影响，但对心灵有什么影响。

sentences.en: I think this type of scarcity is almost like an alarm that goes off in the head that's saying, hey, we really need this thing addressed.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种稀缺就像是在大脑中响起的一个警报，在说：“嘿，我们真的需要解决这个问题。”

sentences.en: We really need this thing addressed. This is Sendhil Mullainathan, a professor of computation and behavioral science at the University of Chicago.
sentences.zh: “我们真的需要解决这个问题。”这是芝加哥大学计算与行为科学教授 Sendhil Mullainathan 说的。

sentences.en: He and a colleague, Eldar Shafir, a psychology professor at Princeton, had a theory brewing.
sentences.zh: 他和普林斯顿大学心理学教授 Eldar Shafir 的同事一直在酝酿一个理论。

sentences.en: It went like this. When you feel that something important is missing in your life, your brain starts to focus on that missing thing.
sentences.zh: 情况是这样的。当你觉得生活中缺少了某个重要的东西时，你的大脑就会开始聚焦于那个缺失的东西。

sentences.en: When you're really desperate for something, you can focus on it so obsessively, there's no room for anything else.
sentences.zh: 当你极度渴望某样东西时，你可以执着到这种程度——以至于容不下其他任何东西。

sentences.en: The researchers were just beginning to explore their hypothesis when a colleague mentioned the long-ago Minnesota starvation experiment.
sentences.zh: 研究人员刚开始探索他们的假设时，一位同事提到了很久以前的明尼苏达饥饿实验。

sentences.en: Eldar remembers being immediately fascinated by the study and how the lack of food affected the minds of the men.
sentences.zh: Eldar 回忆说，他立刻被这项研究以及食物匮乏如何影响这些男人的心理所吸引。

sentences.en: They basically were very hungry and could - couldn't stop thinking about eating.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上非常饥饿，而且——无法停止思考吃东西的事。

sentences.en: You know, in some sense, you'd think, given that they cannot eat, they'd rather be distracted with other things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，从某种意义上说，你可能会想，既然他们吃不到东西，他们宁愿用别的事来转移注意力。

sentences.en: But in fact, both subconsciously, the level of need-it (ph) reaction, and their choice of conversation largely was around food.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，无论是潜意识层面的需求反应，还是他们的谈话主题，很大程度上都围绕着食物。

sentences.en: Actually, it was sort of tragicomic. I mean, they planned to open restaurants, to become restaurateurs.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这有点悲喜剧的意思。我的意思是，他们计划开餐馆，想成为餐馆老板。

sentences.en: They memorized recipes. They compared food prices of different newspapers.
sentences.zh: 他们背诵食谱。他们比较不同报纸上的食物价格。

sentences.en: That's what they were doing. The whole time, they sat around looking at food-related issues.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们在做的事。整整一段时间，他们坐在一起讨论与食物相关的话题。

sentences.en: Even intentional diversions didn't work.
sentences.zh: 就连刻意的转移注意力的尝试也没有奏效。

sentences.en: Hunger and food had captured their minds.
sentences.zh: 饥饿和食物已经占据了他们的心智。

sentences.en: At some point, the experimenters just felt sorry for them and decided to distract them with a movie.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，实验人员实在觉得他们怪可怜的，决定用一部电影来分散他们的注意力。

sentences.en: And some of the testimonials were, they showed me this movie.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人的证言是，他们给我看了这部电影。

sentences.en: I couldn't care less about the love scenes.
sentences.zh: 我才不在乎那些爱情场面呢。

sentences.en: I wanted to see the meals. Eldar suddenly realized he had seen the same kind of behavior in a completely different setting.
sentences.zh: 我想看的是大餐。Eldar 突然意识到他在一个完全不同的环境中见过这种行为。

sentences.en: He'd done a lot of research on the effects of poverty.
sentences.zh: 他做过大量关于贫困影响的研究。

sentences.en: And he knew poor people who sometimes behaved like the starving men in Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 他认识一些穷人，他们的行为有时就像明尼苏达那些挨饿的人一样。

sentences.en: The poor, people who are lacking financial resources, find it very hard to think about anything but money or at least spend a lot of their cognitive resources, a lot of their attention, on financial juggling.
sentences.zh: 穷人，也就是缺乏经济资源的人，发现自己很难去思考金钱以外的任何事情，或者至少把他们大量的认知资源、大量的注意力都花在了财务周旋上。

sentences.en: If starvation made people obsess over food, poverty made people obsess over how they were going to make ends meet, how to make it to next week.
sentences.zh: 如果饥饿让人对食物着迷，那么贫困就让人对如何维持生计、如何撑到下周着迷。

sentences.en: What's in common in both cases is your head is busy with the thing you don't have enough of.
sentences.zh: 两者的共同点在于，你的脑子里全都是你严重缺乏的那样东西。

sentences.en: The two researchers felt they were on to something.
sentences.zh: 这两位研究人员觉得他们有所发现。

sentences.en: Maybe, they thought, the human brain is wired to respond to scarcity by tunnelling in on the thing that's missing.
sentences.zh: 他们想，也许人类的大脑在面对稀缺时，会自动锁定那个缺失的东西。

sentences.en: Sendhil says this makes sense from an evolutionary perspective.
sentences.zh: Sendhil 说，从进化的角度来看，这是合乎情理的。

sentences.en: Picture that you have somebody from 25,000 years ago who's basically a hunter-gatherer and who might need to do a variety of things such as, you know, get water, do - you know, a lot of resources are needed.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，你有一个生活在 25,000 年前的祖先，他基本上是个狩猎采集者，可能需要做各种各样的事情，比如找水，做——你知道的，需要大量的资源。

sentences.en: When they get hungry, it's sort of the evolutionary system wants to have an alarm that says, hey, really focus on getting food into the system.
sentences.zh: 当他们感到饥饿时，进化系统希望发出一个警报，上面写着：“嘿，一定要把精力集中在把食物弄进体内上。”

sentences.en: And that, I think, is the basic scarcity instinct.
sentences.zh: 我想，这就是最基本的稀缺本能。

sentences.en: We're hungry. And then this thing starts going off in the head saying, do you realize we're hungry?
sentences.zh: 我们饿了。然后大脑里就开始有个声音在说：“你意识到我们饿了吗？”

sentences.en: Have I mentioned we're hungry? We're hungry.
sentences.zh: 我提过我们饿了吗？我们饿了。

sentences.en: And it just keeps calling out to you. For Brandy Drew, the alarm might have sounded like this.
sentences.zh: 它一直在对你呼喊。对 Brandy Drew 来说，这个警报听起来可能是这样的。

sentences.en: You don't have the necessities your family needs.
sentences.zh: 你没有你家人需要的必需品。

sentences.en: You need to stock up. Stock up now. You need these things.
sentences.zh: 你需要囤货。马上囤货。你需要这些东西。

sentences.en: And when she bought the bleach, the family-sized pack of toilet paper, the snacks and juice boxes for the kids, the alarm temporarily went silent.
sentences.zh: 当她买下漂白剂、家庭装卫生纸、零食和给孩子们的果汁盒时，警报暂时安静了下来。

sentences.en: I felt relieved that those things - the small things I didn't have to worry about.
sentences.zh: 我感到松了一口气，因为那些事情——那些我不必再为此发愁的小事。

sentences.en: But the reprieve from the alarm came at a huge cost.
sentences.zh: 但警报暂停的代价是巨大的。

sentences.en: But then, like I said, two days later it's like, OK, wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 但正如我所说，两天后感觉就像是，好吧，等等。

sentences.en: Why didn't you save at least $100 for gas?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不至少存100美元来买汽油呢？

sentences.en: The answer to that question, Sandhil and Eldar believe, has to do with what scarcity did to Brandy.
sentences.zh: Sendhil 和 Eldar 认为，这个问题的答案与稀缺对 Brandy 造成的负面影响有关。

sentences.en: She was so focused on getting the basic necessities that she didn't have the mental capacity to attend to anything else.
sentences.zh: 她太专注于获取基本必需品，以至于没有足够的脑力去关注其他任何事情。

sentences.en: There's a technical term for this. It's called bandwidth.
sentences.zh: 这有一个专业术语，叫做带宽。

sentences.en: If you're downloading a movie on your home Wi-Fi network, you might find your email runs a little slower.
sentences.zh: 如果你正在家里的 Wi-Fi 网络上下载电影，你可能会发现你的电子邮件运行得有点慢。

sentences.en: The movie is hogging all the available bandwidth.
sentences.zh: 这部电影占用了所有可用的带宽。

sentences.en: Sendhil and Eldar say our minds work exactly the same way.
sentences.zh: Sendhil 和 Eldar 表示，我们的思维工作原理完全一样。

sentences.en: If your mind is consumed with thoughts about something, there isn't room to think about other stuff.
sentences.zh: 如果你的大脑被关于某件事的想法占据了，就没有空间去思考其他事情了。

sentences.en: Scarcity fills the mind with intrusive thoughts about what you do not have.
sentences.zh: 稀缺让你的大脑充满了关于你所没有的东西的侵入性想法。

sentences.en: It doesn't leave room for anything else.
sentences.zh: 它不给其他任何东西留出空间。

sentences.en: Eldar says there's a simple way to demonstrate this.
sentences.zh: Eldar 说，有一个简单的方法可以证明这一点。

sentences.en: Imagine trying to hold an eight-digit number in your head.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，试着在脑子里记住一个八位数。

sentences.en: And if I simply ask you to keep in mind, you know, 2-6-7-1-7-1-6-4, that just leaves you less able to attend to other stuff.
sentences.zh: 如果我只是让你记住，你知道的，2-6-7-1-7-1-6-4，这只会让你处理其他事情的能力变差。

sentences.en: You eat less well. You pay attention to less things, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 你吃得不那么好。你对周围事物的注意力减少，等等。

sentences.en: As you're saying that eight-digit number now, I didn't hear the rest of the next two sentences because I'm trying to remember that eight-digit number. (Laughter). (Laughter) I won't test you.
sentences.zh: 正如你现在在说那个八位数时，我根本没听清接下来两句话的内容，因为我正努力记住那个八位数。（笑声）。（笑声）我不会考你的。

sentences.en: I promise. But in a sense, that's kind of the metaphor.
sentences.zh: 我保证。但从某种意义上说，这就是一种隐喻。

sentences.en: So when you're busy juggling your resources, worrying about, you know, how am I going to pay for dinner, and if I pay for dinner, will I be able to have money for the kids' school trip, it's like keeping an eight-digit number in your head.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你忙于周旋各种资源，担心着，你知道的，我怎么支付晚饭钱，如果我付了晚饭钱，我还有钱给孩子们交学校春游费吗，这就像在脑子里一直记着一个八位数。

sentences.en: There's a reason our minds work this way.
sentences.zh: 我们的思维以这种方式运作是有原因的。

sentences.en: Tunneling into something makes you focus on it.
sentences.zh: 聚焦于某事会让你全神贯注于它。

sentences.en: Everything inside the tunnel becomes crystal clear.
sentences.zh: 隧道里的一切变得一清二楚。

sentences.en: The problem is you can't see anything outside the tunnel.
sentences.zh: 问题是你看不见隧道外面的任何东西。

sentences.en: People in the poverty tunnel are actually very good at figuring out how to stretch the money they have to make it to tomorrow or the next week.
sentences.zh: 身处贫困隧道中的人们实际上非常擅长弄清楚如何精打细算利用手头的钱，撑到明天或下周。

sentences.en: Studies show that the poor tend to be better than the rich at knowing where you can find the best deals, the cheap tube of toothpaste.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，穷人往往比富人更擅长寻找最划算的交易、更便宜的牙膏。

sentences.en: Someone who is poor is often consumed with finding solutions to immediate problems.
sentences.zh: 一个贫困的人往往满脑子都在寻找眼前问题的解决方案。

sentences.en: How do I get food on the table today? I'm not thinking about problems that are a few weeks away, like the utility bill or gas money or a credit card payment.
sentences.zh: 我今天怎么把饭弄上桌？我才不会去想几周后的问题，比如水电费、汽油费或信用卡还款。

sentences.en: As you - as you're checking the prices and remembering the prices and figuring out if you buy two carrots, will you have enough money for breakfast, you are forgetting things.
sentences.zh: 当你在——当你核对价格、记住价格、琢磨着如果你买两根胡萝卜，你是否有足够的钱吃早饭时，你正在忘记其他事情。

sentences.en: You're paying less attention to your rent, to your kids' homework, to all of the other things that make, you know, life complete.
sentences.zh: 你对房租、孩子的家庭作业以及所有让生活变得完整的事情的关注变少了。

sentences.en: The thing is, as a result of doing this, the underlying problem can become worse.
sentences.zh: 问题是，这样做的结果是，潜在的问题可能会变得更糟。

sentences.en: If you don't pay your bills, you'll be even deeper in the hole next month.
sentences.zh: 如果你不付账单，下个月你就会陷入更深的泥潭。

sentences.en: Scarcity, in other words, is a trap. The scarcity trap for us is all those ways in which scarcity today begets behaviors, which leads to even further scarcity tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，稀缺是一个陷阱。对我们而言，稀缺陷阱是指今天的一切稀缺行径会引发各种行为，进而导致明天更严重的稀缺。

sentences.en: And we think it's something that poor people do, busy people do.
sentences.zh: 我们以为这是穷人和大忙人才会做的事。

sentences.en: Here's another example. We think the lonely do this.
sentences.zh: 这里还有另一个例子。我们认为孤独的人也会这样。

sentences.en: So people who are lonely will often engage in social interactions in a particular way, which actually makes it harder for them to make friends.
sentences.zh: 所以孤独的人往往会以某种特定方式参与社交互动，这实际上使他们更难交到朋友。

sentences.en: Just as the poor focus on the money they do not have, the lonely tend to focus on the friends they do not have.
sentences.zh: 正如穷人专注于他们没有的钱一样，孤独的人往往专注于他们没有的朋友。

sentences.en: The result is they try too hard to be liked.
sentences.zh: 结果就是他们表现得太渴望被喜欢了。

sentences.en: In a conversation, the lonely person might be so preoccupied with making a good impression that he can't pay attention to what's actually being said.
sentences.zh: 在谈话中，孤独的人可能会全神贯注于留下好印象，以至于无法专注于对方实际在说的话。

sentences.en: The conversation falters. Instead of appearing likable, he's seen as awkward or flatfooted.
sentences.zh: 谈话冷场了。他没有显得讨人喜欢，反而被视为笨拙或不合群。

sentences.en: What happens as a result? People avoid the awkward conversationalist, and the lonely person becomes even lonelier.
sentences.zh: 结果会怎样？人们避开这个言谈笨拙的人，而孤独的人变得更加孤独。

sentences.en: This lens offers a new way of thinking about why people who find themselves in scarcity seem to do things that to an outsider look stupid.
sentences.zh: 这种视角为思考为什么陷入稀缺的人会做出在外人看来很愚蠢的事情提供了一种新方法。

sentences.en: When you're in a hole, why would you dig yourself even deeper?
sentences.zh: 当你身处泥潭时，为什么还要把自己挖得更深？

sentences.en: Sendhil says we're asking the wrong question.
sentences.zh: Sendhil 说我们问错了问题。

sentences.en: What if it's not that poor people are somehow deficient but that poverty makes everyone less capable?
sentences.zh: 如果不是穷人在某种程度上有所欠缺，而是贫穷让每个人都变得能力不足呢？

sentences.en: That it's the - it's - you and I, tomorrow, were we to become poor, would all of a sudden have the same effect, that poverty is in some sense changing our minds.
sentences.zh: 那就是——那就是——你和我，如果在明天变得穷困潦倒，突然之间也会产生同样的效果，贫穷在某种程度上改变了我们的思维。

sentences.en: How do we know this isn't some bleeding heart theory to excuse irresponsible behavior?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么知道这不是某种为不负责任行为开脱的滥情理论呢？

sentences.en: Eldar and Sendhil wanted to test their hypothesis.
sentences.zh: Eldar 和 Sendhil 想检验他们的假设。

sentences.en: If all this is true, one thing that ought to be true is the same person when they're poor should have very different cognitive capacity than when they're rich.
sentences.zh: 如果这一切都是真的，那么有一点应该是真的：同一个人在贫穷时的认知能力应该与富裕时大不相同。

sentences.en: So how would we test that? Well, unfortunately we don't have the kind of money to go around making poor people rich.
sentences.zh: 那么我们该如何检验这一点呢？不幸的是，我们没有那么多钱去把穷人变成富人。

sentences.en: But sugar cane farmers actually create a natural experiment for us.
sentences.zh: 但甘蔗农实际上为我们创造了一个自然实验。

sentences.en: Yes, sugar cane farmers, specifically those in India who are paid only once a year, right after the harvest.
sentences.zh: 是的，甘蔗农，特别是印度的甘蔗农，他们一年只在收获后领一次工资。

sentences.en: The month after they get that income, they're pretty rich.
sentences.zh: 拿到收入后的那个月，他们相当富有。

sentences.en: But like anybody who gets a huge windfall all at once, the money gets spent a little too fast.
sentences.zh: 但就像任何一下子获得巨额意外之财的人一样，钱花得有点太快了。

sentences.en: And so by the end of the harvest cycle, they're relatively poor.
sentences.zh: 因此，到收获周期的末尾，他们相对来说就变穷了。

sentences.en: So now we have the same person, a month before harvest, poor, and a month after harvest, well-off.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们有了同一个人，收获前一个月很穷，收获后一个月很富裕。

sentences.en: Again, you have the same group of people who are poor one moment and rich the next.
sentences.zh: 同样，你拥有同一群人在某个时刻贫穷而在另一个时刻富裕。

sentences.en: Sendhil and Eldar tested the farmers on their long-term thinking when they had no money and when they had plenty of money.
sentences.zh: Sendhil 和 Eldar 在这些农民身无分文和手头宽裕时，对他们的长远思考能力进行了测试。

sentences.en: The results were stunning. We found a huge difference.
sentences.zh: 结果令人惊叹。我们发现了巨大的差异。

sentences.en: So we found that post-harvest, when they're well-off, they have much more impulse control.
sentences.zh: 因此我们发现，在收获后他们手头宽裕时，他们有更强的冲动控制力。

sentences.en: Farmers who were rich tended to think about things that would help them over the long term.
sentences.zh: 富裕起来的农民往往会考虑那些对他们长远有帮助的事情。

sentences.en: This matched other research that shows, for example, that farmers who are well-off tend to weed their fields more regularly than farmers who are poor.
sentences.zh: 这与其他的研究所显示的相吻合，例如，手头宽裕的农民往往比贫穷的农民更经常地给田地除草。

sentences.en: Farmers who were poor mostly focused on how to make it to next week - short-term thinking.
sentences.zh: 贫穷的农民主要关注如何撑到下周——短视思维。

sentences.en: To be clear, it's not that poor people focus on immediate needs because that's all they want to think about.
sentences.zh: 需要明确的是，并不是说穷人只关注眼前需求，因为那是他们唯一想考虑的。

sentences.en: It's all they can think about. Scarcity captures the mind, like it did with those starving men in Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 那是他们唯一能考虑的。稀缺抓住了大脑，就像明尼苏达那些挨饿的人一样。

sentences.en: In fact, scarcity can actually lower how you perform on an IQ test.
sentences.zh: 事实上，稀缺实际上会拉低你的智商测试成绩。

sentences.en: Put simply, being poor is like having just pulled an all-nighter.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，贫穷就像刚熬了个通宵一样。

sentences.en: Now, if you've been very lucky, maybe you've never experienced what it's like to be poor or hungry or lonely.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你很幸运，你可能从未体验过贫穷、饥饿或孤独的滋味。

sentences.en: But there might be another form of scarcity you have experienced.
sentences.zh: 但你可能体验过另一种形式的稀缺。

sentences.en: On some days, we get to leave at 4 p.m. Some days, we don't leave till 1 a.m. (Laughter).
sentences.zh: 有时候我们可以下午4点下班。有时我们直到凌晨1点才离开。（笑声）。

sentences.en: So - and then you usually start the next day at 5:30 or 6 in the morning, usually work 80 hours-ish (ph) a week.
sentences.zh: 所以——然后你通常在第二天早上5点半或6点开始，通常一周工作80个小时左右。

sentences.en: When we come back, how being overworked and exhausted can produce a form of scarcity too and the pernicious effect this can have on your life.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们将探讨过度劳累和精疲力竭如何同样产生一种稀缺，以及它对你生活产生的恶劣影响。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续关注。

sentences.en: Eldar Shafir and Sendhil Mullainathan believe that when something you desperately need is in short supply, your brain tends to focus on that thing.
sentences.zh: Eldar Shafir 和 Sendhil Mullainathan 认为，当你急需的某样东西供应短缺时，你的大脑往往会专注于该东西。

sentences.en: This focus can be so intense that it impedes your ability to think about anything else.
sentences.zh: 这种专注可以如此强烈，以至于阻碍了你思考其他任何事情的能力。

sentences.en: What happens when the thing you're missing is time, when you're so busy it feels like you don't have time to breathe?
sentences.zh: 当你在缺少时间、忙得连喘气的时间都没有时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: Let me tell you the story of a young woman named Katie (ph).
sentences.zh: 让我给你们讲一个叫 Katie 的年轻女性的故事。

sentences.en: She asked us to use her middle name for reasons that will be clear in a moment.
sentences.zh: 她要求我们使用她的中间名，原因一会儿就会明了。

sentences.en: For as long as she can remember, Katie has been driven - really driven.
sentences.zh: 在她记事起，Katie 就一直很有进取心——非常拼。

sentences.en: When I was in high school, I was determined to be valedictorian, so I took a sophomore-level honors biology course as a freshman in high school.
sentences.zh: 当我上高中的时候，我决心成为毕业典礼致辞代表（valedictorian），所以我在高一的时候就选修了大学二年级的荣誉生物课。

sentences.en: And I studied around the clock. I had note cards.
sentences.zh: 我不分昼夜地学习。我有小卡片。

sentences.en: I walked through the hallways with the note cards.
sentences.zh: 我拿着小卡片走在走廊里。

sentences.en: If there was a holiday party, I brought the note cards.
sentences.zh: 如果有节日派对，我也带着小卡片。

sentences.en: And I'd also study till 2 or 3 in the morning.
sentences.zh: 我甚至学到凌晨2点或3点。

sentences.en: Katie says she wanted to be perfect at school.
sentences.zh: Katie 说她想在学校里做到完美。

sentences.en: She eventually got to medical school, where she excelled.
sentences.zh: 她最终进入了医学院，并在那里表现优异。

sentences.en: She graduated at the top of her class and quickly started her residency.
sentences.zh: 她以优异的成绩毕业，并迅速开始了自己的住院医师实习期。

sentences.en: The new schedule was grueling. You can get in at 5:30 or 6 in the morning, and you round on all your patients.
sentences.zh: 新的日程安排极其折磨人。你早上5点半或6点到医院，然后对所有病人进行查房。

sentences.en: And then you - you round with the team. That means you go to all the patients and check in on their plan and adjust medications, et cetera, as necessary.
sentences.zh: 然后你——你和团队一起查房。这意味着你要去看所有的病人，检查他们的治疗方案，并根据需要调整药物等。

sentences.en: And then there's usually a lunch conference, where we have education.
sentences.zh: 然后通常有一个午餐会议，我们在那里接受教育。

sentences.en: And then in the afternoon, we might take new patients in and keep following up on our patients.
sentences.zh: 下午，我们可能会接收新病人，并继续跟进我们的病人。

sentences.en: And on some days, we get to leave at 4 p.m.
sentences.zh: 有时候我们可以下午4点离开。

sentences.en: Some days, we don't leave till 1 a.m. (Laughter).
sentences.zh: 有时候我们直到凌晨1点才离开。（笑声）。

sentences.en: So - and then you usually start the next day at 5:30 or 6 in the morning again.
sentences.zh: 所以——然后你通常第二天早上5点半或6点又开始。

sentences.en: And you get one day off a week, usually work 80 hours-ish a week.
sentences.zh: 你一周有一天假，通常一周工作80个小时左右。

sentences.en: As Katie's workload grew, she started to feel she couldn't afford to waste a single moment.
sentences.zh: 随着 Katie 的工作量增加，她开始觉得自己浪费不起哪怕一分钱的时刻。

sentences.en: Instead of spending any time relaxing, she started to focus only on things directly related to her success at work.
sentences.zh: 她没有把任何时间花在放松上，而是开始只专注于那些与她在工作中取得成功直接相关的事情。

sentences.en: When I first started, it was just, like, really busy.
sentences.zh: 刚开始的时候，就是，感觉真的很忙。

sentences.en: So I'd try to come home, and I felt like, you know, I just don't have a lot of hours.
sentences.zh: 所以我试图回家，我觉得，你知道的，我没有很多时间。

sentences.en: So I need to make the most of them and was like, OK, I need to make sure I'm exercising, keeping my body healthy.
sentences.zh: 所以我需要充分利用它们，心想，好吧，我得确保我在锻炼，保持身体健康。

sentences.en: And I need to read and stay on top of things.
sentences.zh: 我需要阅读并跟上各种进度。

sentences.en: So I'd come home after a pretty long day, and I might go walking for half an hour.
sentences.zh: 所以我会在漫长的一天结束后回家，可能会去散步半小时。

sentences.en: And then I'd read. And then I'd go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 然后我阅读。然后我去睡觉。

sentences.en: But then, as the time went on, I decided to try to get in more exercise 'cause I'm like, I never know when I'll get enough exercise in.
sentences.zh: 但后来，随着时间的推移，我决定做更多运动，因为我想，我永远不知道什么时候才能得到足够的锻炼。

sentences.en: So I started spending all my free daylight hours walking or running outside or going to the gym, up to three hours a day, plus, like, working 15-hour days and then trying to read and then go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始把我所有的白天空闲时间都花在户外散步、跑步或去健身房上，每天长达三个小时，再加上工作15小时，还要看书，然后睡觉。

sentences.en: As she focused intensely on the things she believed were key to her professional success, Katie lost sight of things on the periphery.
sentences.zh: 由于她全神贯注于她认为是自己职业成功关键的事情，Katie 忽略了周围的其他事情。

sentences.en: She didn't know it, but she was entering the tunnel of scarcity.
sentences.zh: 她自己并不知道，但她正在步入稀缺的隧道。

sentences.en: In her case, it was scarcity brought on by a lack of time.
sentences.zh: 对她而言，这是缺乏时间所带来的稀缺。

sentences.en: So I wasn't going to the grocery store. My house wasn't unpacked yet.
sentences.zh: 所以我没有去杂货店。我的房子还没拆包。

sentences.en: And it was stressing me out. And it was just a mess.
sentences.zh: 这让我压力很大。真是一团糟。

sentences.en: And I've - my clothes piled up. I had a lot of dirty clothes.
sentences.zh: 而且我的衣服堆成了山。我有很多脏衣服。

sentences.en: And coming home just felt so overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 回到家感觉太让人喘不过气了。

sentences.en: I didn't want to be there. And that's part of, I think, why I was walking so much, just to get out of the house and get away from all the things I hadn't done.
sentences.zh: 我不想待在那里。我想这也是为什么我走那么多路的部分原因，只是为了离开家，远离那些我还没做完的事情。

sentences.en: And I also forgot to pay a bill in the midst of all of this.
sentences.zh: 在这一切焦头烂额中，我还忘记付账单了。

sentences.en: What did you forget to do? What bill did you forget to pay?
sentences.zh: 你忘记做什么了？你忘记付什么账单了？

sentences.en: It was my energy bill. The old Katie would have spotted all of this.
sentences.zh: 是我的电费账单。过去的 Katie 本来会注意到这一切的。

sentences.en: I mean, you were just basically, at this point, almost falling apart it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听起来你当时基本上快要崩溃了。

sentences.en: I was. I was falling apart. There was something else.
sentences.zh: 我是。我快崩溃了。还有别的事。

sentences.en: Katie had battled anorexia as a teenager.
sentences.zh: Katie 在青少年时期曾与神经性厌食症作斗争。

sentences.en: She knew she had to stay vigilant about her eating.
sentences.zh: 她知道她必须对自己的饮食保持警惕。

sentences.en: But as she started to focus ever more intensely on work, she slipped back into some old habits.
sentences.zh: 但随着她越来越专注于工作，她又滑回了一些旧习惯。

sentences.en: I was eating mostly vegetables and fruits.
sentences.zh: 我主要吃蔬菜和水果。

sentences.en: And I wasn't eating a whole lot else, maybe a Clif bar here and there.
sentences.zh: 我没吃多少其他东西，也许偶尔吃一根 Clif 能量棒。

sentences.en: Despite all her medical training, Katie stopped taking care of herself.
sentences.zh: 尽管受过所有的医学培训，Katie 却停止了自我照顾。

sentences.en: Here's one thing I haven't told you yet about scarcity.
sentences.zh: 关于稀缺，我还有一件事没告诉你。

sentences.en: It can rob you of insight, insight about how your own mind is changing.
sentences.zh: 它会剥夺你的洞察力，让你对自己的思维如何发生变化失去洞察力。

sentences.en: Katie had no awareness that she was heading down a dangerous path.
sentences.zh: Katie 完全没有意识到自己正在走向一条危险的道路。

sentences.en: It became obvious to her only when it finally affected her work.
sentences.zh: 直到它最终影响到她的工作，她才意识到这一点。

sentences.en: I started to notice that I was, like, nearly missing things as I was reviewing.
sentences.zh: 我开始注意到，我在复查时，险些漏掉一些东西。

sentences.en: For example, I admitted a diabetic. And I almost didn't order insulin for them.
sentences.zh: 例如，我收治了一位糖尿病患者。我差点没给他们开胰岛素。

sentences.en: But I did order the insulin. But I was like, I don't think I can keep up with this anymore because if you don't give a diabetic insulin - especially if they're Type 1 - they can have very fatal circumstances in the hospital and get really high blood sugars that can cause them to have an acidosis and end up on a ventilator.
sentences.zh: 但我最终还是开了胰岛素。不过我想，我再也无法承受这种压力了，因为如果你不给糖尿病患者胰岛素——特别是如果他们是1型糖尿病患者——他们在医院里可能会遭遇致命的情况，血糖极高，导致酮症酸中毒，并最终用上呼吸机。

sentences.en: So I turned myself in at the point that I saw that it was starting to affect my work.
sentences.zh: 所以当我发现它开始影响我的工作时，我主动向医院上报了。

sentences.en: In two months of the residency program, Katie's body and mind had withered.
sentences.zh: 在住院医师培训项目的两个月里，Katie 的身心都日渐枯萎。

sentences.en: Things had gotten so bad, she had to go to a residential treatment center.
sentences.zh: 情况变得如此糟糕，她不得不去了一家住宅式治疗中心。

sentences.en: Katie struggled with two things. Her body was desperately in need of nutrition.
sentences.zh: Katie 与两件事做斗争。她的身体迫切需要营养。

sentences.en: And her mind, she had to find a way to stop the intrusive thoughts that were consuming her.
sentences.zh: 而她的精神，她必须找到一种方法来阻止那些消耗她的侵入性想法。

sentences.en: She had to... Learn how to just sit because we weren't allowed to exercise.
sentences.zh: 她必须……学会只是坐着，因为我们不允许锻炼。

sentences.en: We weren't allowed to stand. We weren't even allowed to do jumping jacks or squats.
sentences.zh: 我们不允许站着。我们甚至不允许做开合跳或深蹲。

sentences.en: We had to just sit. Katie's mind was filled with angry and impatient thoughts.
sentences.zh: 我们只能坐着。Katie 的脑子里充满了愤怒和不耐烦的想法。

sentences.en: At first, I felt like - I felt useless because I thought, you know, if I'm not doing something productive, what is my purpose in life?
sentences.zh: 起初，我觉得——我觉得自己很没用，因为我想，你知道的，如果我没有做一些有成效的事情，我生活的意义是什么？

sentences.en: But gradually, as the program literally forced her to do nothing, Katie started to emerge from the tunnel.
sentences.zh: 但渐渐地，随着该项目实际上强迫她什么都不做，Katie 开始走出隧道。

sentences.en: She realized she had been so narrowly, relentlessly focused on one goal, doing well at work, that she had ignored the very things she needed to succeed - moments of relaxation, like watching TV or, in her case, painting.
sentences.zh: 她意识到自己曾如此狭隘、无休止地专注于一个目标——在工作中表现出色，以至于她忽视了自己取得成功真正需要的东西——放松的时刻，比如看电视，或者对她而言，画画。

sentences.en: Katie had loved art as a child, but she had put it aside because she thought it wouldn't help her become a better doctor.
sentences.zh: Katie 小时候很喜欢艺术，但她把它搁置了一边，因为她认为这无助于她成为一名更好的医生。

sentences.en: I'm kind of the type of person that just likes to study and then do after I've, like, mastered it from a study point of view.
sentences.zh: 我是那种喜欢先学习，然后在从学习的角度掌握之后再去实践的人。

sentences.en: And so to just do something without instruction is - it feels very vulnerable to me.
sentences.zh: 所以在没有任何指导的情况下做一件事——这让我感觉非常脆弱。

sentences.en: But it ended up kind of being my saving grace in my recovery.
sentences.zh: 但它最终成为了我康复过程中的救命稻草。

sentences.en: And I've actually created an art room in my house.
sentences.zh: 我实际上在家里创建了一个艺术室。

sentences.en: I changed my office from a work room into an art room.
sentences.zh: 我把办公室从工作间改成了艺术室。

sentences.en: And it has paints and watercolors and chalks and everything you can imagine.
sentences.zh: 里面有颜料、水彩、粉笔以及你能想象到的一切。

sentences.en: And I try to go in there once a week and just create something without any expectation, just for the purpose of creating it because I can.
sentences.zh: 我试着每周去一次，不抱任何期望地创作点东西，仅仅为了创作而创作，因为我能。

sentences.en: Katie eventually returned to her residency program with a new outlook.
sentences.zh: Katie 最终以崭新的面貌回到了她的住院医师项目。

sentences.en: She started doing something that Eldar and Sendhil recommend to all busy people.
sentences.zh: 她开始做 Eldar 和 Sendhil 推荐给所有大忙人的事情。

sentences.en: She actually pencils time into her schedule to do nothing.
sentences.zh: 她实际上把“什么都不做”的时间写进了日程表。

sentences.en: One of the big things I've done is I kind of have a date night with myself once or twice a week, where I just schedule off the night.
sentences.zh: 我所做的最重要的事情之一就是，我每周或每两周给自己安排一次约会，把那天晚上的时间空出来。

sentences.en: And I won't do anything with anyone else.
sentences.zh: 而且我不会和任何人一起做任何事。

sentences.en: And it'll just be free for me to do what I feel like.
sentences.zh: 这段时间完全由我自由支配，做我想做的事。

sentences.en: It might be watching a movie. It might be taking a soak in the tub and reading a book or being in my art room and painting whatever comes to me.
sentences.zh: 可能是看电影。可能是泡个澡读本书，或者待在艺术室里画任何涌上心头的东西。

sentences.en: But I do - like, I prioritize that. And I actually won't accept plans with friends, generally, when I do this.
sentences.zh: 但我确实——比如，我把这放在首位。而且通常情况下，我不会接受朋友的邀约。

sentences.en: So that's one of the things I do. Katie is consciously freeing up bandwidth.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所做的事情之一。Katie 正在有意识地释放带宽。

sentences.en: And something strange has happened as she's done so.
sentences.zh: 随着她的这样做，一件奇怪的事情发生了。

sentences.en: The less consumed she feels about work, the better she does at work.
sentences.zh: 她对工作的执念越少，她在工作中的表现就越好。

sentences.en: Honestly, like, it's kind of incredible.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这简直有点不可思议。

sentences.en: But at work, my brain has increased its capacity fourfold.
sentences.zh: 但在工作中，我的大脑容量增加了四倍。

sentences.en: I am able to hold so many more things in my consciousness at once and manage them.
sentences.zh: 我能够同时在意识中容纳更多的东西并加以管理。

sentences.en: I've just seen a really huge improvement in my ability to enjoy being in the company of others, to enjoy, like, occasions and to enjoy my work and do well at my work.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己享受他人陪伴的能力、享受场合的能力以及享受工作并在工作中表现出色的能力都有了非常巨大的提升。

sentences.en: While the psychological studies into scarcity and bandwidth are relatively new, the ideas are actually ancient.
sentences.zh: 虽然关于稀缺和带宽的心理学研究相对较新，但这些理念其实由来已久。

sentences.en: Avoid tunnel vision. Keep difficult things in one part of your life from contaminating everything else.
sentences.zh: 避免管窥效应。把生活中某个部分的难题与其余部分隔离开来。

sentences.en: Be present. Say you have a big deadline tomorrow for something you've got to finish.
sentences.zh: 活在当下。假设你明天有一个必须完成的重大截止日期。

sentences.en: You go home, and you're spending the evening with your kids.
sentences.zh: 你回到家，正和孩子们共度傍晚时光。

sentences.en: And in that moment, you're not present-focused at all.
sentences.zh: 而在那一刻，你根本没有专注于当下。

sentences.en: What you're focused on is that deadline.
sentences.zh: 你专注于的是那个截止日期。

sentences.en: You - you may go through minutes where you didn't hear what your kids were saying to you because your mind keeps going to this other thing.
sentences.zh: 你——你可能会有好几分钟根本没听清孩子们在对你说什么，因为你的大脑一直在想别的事。

sentences.en: Tunnel vision is not in itself a good thing or a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 管窥效应本身并非好事或坏事。

sentences.en: Shutting out distractions can be helpful at times.
sentences.zh: 屏蔽干扰有时会很有帮助。

sentences.en: The question is, do you know when you're inside the tunnel?
sentences.zh: 问题是，你知道自己什么时候身处隧道之中吗？

sentences.en: To me, that's exactly the heart of managing scarcity.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这正是管理稀缺的核心所在。

sentences.en: It's recognizing when you're trying to do something related to your scarcity where you really want to use that instinct.
sentences.zh: 它在于识别你什么时候在做与稀缺相关的事情，此时你确实想运用那种本能。

sentences.en: And when have you made a conscious decision to do something else where what you really need to do is to not have it intrude on that something else?
sentences.zh: 以及什么时候你做出了有意识的决定去做别的事，而你真正需要做的是不让它侵入到那件别的事中？

sentences.en: You're at home. You're with your kids. You chose to be a parent for that three-hour period.
sentences.zh: 你在家里。你和孩子们在一起。你在那三个小时里选择做一个父母。

sentences.en: You really don't want scarcity to intrude then.
sentences.zh: 你真的不希望稀缺在那时入侵。

sentences.en: Of course, it's easy to say, build free time into your schedule.
sentences.zh: 当然，说起来容易，在日程中安排出自由时间。

sentences.en: Stay present with your family. Take a vacation.
sentences.zh: 与家人保持当下的连结。去度假。

sentences.en: These strategies presume you have choices.
sentences.zh: 这些策略的前提是你还有得选。

sentences.en: You can't say, I've had it with being lonely.
sentences.zh: 你不能说，我受够这种孤独了。

sentences.en: I'm going to take a vacation from being lonely.
sentences.zh: 我要去对孤独放个假。

sentences.en: It's not a choice. And to me, loneliness and poverty are the forms of scarcity that feel the biggest because while all these forces are at play, there's no release valve.
sentences.zh: 这不是一种选择。对我和来说，孤独和贫困是感觉最巨大的两种稀缺形态，因为在所有这些力量交织起作用的时候，并没有一个释放阀。

sentences.en: There's no escape mechanism. Eldar and Sendhil want policymakers to design solutions that recognize how scarcity creates traps from which many people may not be able to extricate themselves.
sentences.zh: 没有逃生机制。Eldar 和 Sendhil 希望政策制定者设计出这样的解决方案：认识到稀缺是如何制造出许多人可能无法自拔的陷阱的。

sentences.en: And they want the rest of us to stop preaching to those in poverty.
sentences.zh: 他们希望我们其余的人停止向处于贫困中的人说教。

sentences.en: If you look at programs of poverty, we often confound a little bit the attempts to help the poor with the attempts to educate them, make sure that they show up on time, that they do the right things.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看那些扶贫项目，我们经常把帮扶穷人的尝试，跟教育他们、确保他们准时出现、让他们做正确事情的尝试混为一谈。

sentences.en: From the perspective we're taking with scarcity, in some sense, if I'm very busy juggling a very complicated life, insisting that I show up at the office at 8 and not 8:05 is not doing me a favor.
sentences.zh: 从我们看待稀缺的角度来看，某种程度上，如果我正忙于应付一个极其复杂的生活，硬性坚持要求我必须在 8 点而不是 8 点 05 分到办公室，这并不是在帮我的忙。

sentences.en: I don't need to be educated. It's just hard to manage.
sentences.zh: 我不需要被教育。这只是很难应付。

sentences.en: I'm - you know, it's just the transportation is not reliable.
sentences.zh: 我——你知道的，只是交通不太可靠。

sentences.en: My kid is not ready. I don't have a babysitter.
sentences.zh: 我的孩子还没准备好。我没有保姆。

sentences.en: I'm going to make mistakes. It's not clear "educating me," in quotes, about things is going to help me at all.
sentences.zh: 我会犯错。关于各种事情“教育我”（加引号的），究竟能不能帮到我，这一点很不确定。

sentences.en: It just makes my life all the more complicated.
sentences.zh: 这只会让我的生活更加复杂。

sentences.en: When people in poverty fail or make mistakes, the researchers think we should respond to them the same way we respond to mistakes made by airline pilots.
sentences.zh: 当处于贫困中的人失败或犯错时，研究人员认为我们应该以对待航空飞行员犯错相同的方式来对待他们。

sentences.en: There was a time not long ago when we thought that airline pilots who made mistakes were just bad pilots.
sentences.zh: 不久前曾有那么一段时间，我们认为犯错的飞行员只是糟糕的飞行员。

sentences.en: Sendhil says a big reason air travel has become safer in recent decades is that there has been a shift in thinking about such mistakes.
sentences.zh: Sendhil 说，近几十年来航空旅行变得更安全的一个主要原因，是对这类错误的看法发生了转变。

sentences.en: Designers have made cockpits fault-tolerant.
sentences.zh: 设计人员已经让驾驶舱具备了容错能力。

sentences.en: Rather than trying to find perfect pilots, cockpits are now designed to account for human error.
sentences.zh: 与其试图找到完美的飞行员，现在的驾驶舱设计已经将人为错误考虑在内。

sentences.en: The goal is to alert pilots when they've made a mistake and to diminish the consequences of mistakes.
sentences.zh: 目标是在飞行员犯错时发出警报，并减轻错误带来的后果。

sentences.en: It's ironic that when we design cockpits, the entire mantra of fault tolerance seems so intuitive.
sentences.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，当我们设计驾驶舱时，容错的整套信条似乎是如此直观。

sentences.en: But when we design social policies, nobody's out there talking about, let's make this fault-tolerant.
sentences.zh: 但是当我们设计社会政策时，却没有人出来谈论，让我们把这个设计成容错的吧。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, poor people have a lot on their mind.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，穷人要操心的事情很多。

sentences.en: Their bandwidth is taxed. They're going to make mistakes.
sentences.zh: 他们的精力心智被榨干了。他们难免会犯错。

sentences.en: Let's make sure this program is robust when they do make that mistake.
sentences.zh: 让我们确保这个项目在他们犯错时依然能够稳健运行。

sentences.en: It's just not the way we think. If I offer a training program, I don't sit there and say, let me make sure - you know, what's going to happen?
sentences.zh: 我们思考的方式根本不是这样的。如果我提供一个培训项目，我不会坐在那里想，让我确保——你知道的，会发生什么？

sentences.en: This is for low-income individuals. Surely, they're going to miss a few days because, you know, it's hard to get get to class sometimes or other things are on their mind.
sentences.zh: 这是面向低收入人群的。当然，他们肯定会缺席几天，因为，你知道的，有时候很难去上课，或者他们心里还要应付别的事。

sentences.en: So let me design this curriculum so that it's in-attendance (ph) tolerant.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我来设计这个课程，让它对出勤具有容忍度（ph）。

sentences.en: So even if somebody misses three days in a row, they'll be able to come on that fourth day and still feel caught up.
sentences.zh: 这样，即使有人连续缺席三天，他们也能在第四天来上课，并且仍然觉得能跟上进度。

sentences.en: In fact, our training curriculum is often quite the opposite.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们的培训课程往往恰恰相反。

sentences.en: If you miss three days in a row, it's an invitation to miss the fourth day because you're not going to get anything.
sentences.zh: 如果你连续缺席三天，这就是在邀请你缺席第四天，因为你什么也学不到了。

sentences.en: Brandy Drew eventually turned her life around.
sentences.zh: Brandy Drew 最终扭转了她的人生。

sentences.en: She found a low-income assistance program that offered her help.
sentences.zh: 她找到一个为她提供帮助的低收入援助项目。

sentences.en: She worked with a financial counselor who gave her strategies for budgeting her money and keeping track of long-term priorities.
sentences.zh: 她和一位财务顾问合作，后者为她提供了如何规划预算和跟进长期优先事项的策略。

sentences.en: I actually have a calendar now that I write down everything to make sure I'm paying things on the correct day and time.
sentences.zh: 我现在确实有一个日历，我把所有东西都写在上面，以确保我在正确的日期和时间支付各项账单。

sentences.en: It's taken time and little steps, but Brandy is no longer in the scarcity tunnel.
sentences.zh: 这需要时间和小步的积累，但 Brandy 终于走出了稀缺的隧道。

sentences.en: She's been working for two years now. And she has savings.
sentences.zh: 她已经工作两年了。并且她有了储蓄。

sentences.en: I know that if anything happens - God forbid, if I lose this job - I know that I can survive for at least six months if I have to look for another.
sentences.zh: 我知道如果发生任何事——上帝保佑，如果我失去了这份工作——我知道如果我不得不寻找另一份工作，我可以至少存活六个月。

sentences.en: Eldar and Sendhil themselves say they are constantly trying to keep the lessons of scarcity front and center in their own lives.
sentences.zh: Eldar 和 Sendhil 自己也说，他们一直在努力将稀缺的教训放在他们自己生活的核心和显眼位置。

sentences.en: As a busy academic, Eldar has come up with a rule.
sentences.zh: 作为一名忙碌的学者，Eldar 想出了一条规则。

sentences.en: When an invitation to an event two months down the road comes along, he asks himself whether he would attend the event if it were tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 当两个月后的某个活动邀请到来时，他会问自己，如果这个活动是明天举行，他还会不会去参加。

sentences.en: If the answer is no, he declines the invitation because his life is not going to be any less hectic two months from now.
sentences.zh: 如果答案是否定的，他就会拒绝邀请，因为他的生活在两个月后也不会变得不那么忙碌。

sentences.en: Preserving bandwidth takes conscious effort.
sentences.zh: 保持精力心智需要有意识的努力。

sentences.en: Most of us, Eldar included, are going to violate the Eldar rule.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人，包括 Eldar 在内，都会违反 Eldar 规则。

sentences.en: We'll say yes to new commitments when we don't have the time or pull out a credit card when we can't afford it.
sentences.zh: 当我们没有时间时，我们会对新的承诺说“好”，或者在我们负担不起时掏出信用卡。

sentences.en: In those moments, it's important to look up to notice we are inside a tunnel.
sentences.zh: 在那些时刻，抬头注意到我们正身处隧道之中至关重要。

sentences.en: This episode was produced by Jenny Schmidt and Maggie Penman.
sentences.zh: 本期节目由 Jenny Schmidt 和 Maggie Penman 制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Tara Boyle. We had original music this week from Ramtin Arablouei.
sentences.zh: 本期节目由 Tara Boyle 剪辑。本期我们的原创音乐来自 Ramtin Arablouei。

sentences.en: Our team includes Rhaina Cohen, Laura Kwerel, Thomas Lu and Parth Shah.
sentences.zh: 我们的团队包括 Rhaina Cohen、Laura Kwerel、Thomas Lu 和 Parth Shah。

sentences.en: Our unsung hero this week is Seung Kim. Seung is a senior director with the Local Initiatives Support Coalition.
sentences.zh: 我们本周的无名英雄是 Seung Kim。Seung 是地方倡议支持联盟（Local Initiatives Support Coalition）的高级主任。

sentences.en: This is a national group that supports financial opportunity centers around the country, including the one in Detroit that helped Brandy Drew get back on her feet.
sentences.zh: 这是一个全国性的组织，支持全国各地的金融机会中心，包括帮助 Brandy Drew 重新站起来的底特律那个中心。

sentences.en: Seung got us in touch with Brandy after making numerous calls and reaching out to friends, colleagues and counselors.
sentences.zh: Seung 在打了无数个电话、联系了朋友、同事和顾问后，帮我们联系上了 Brandy。

sentences.en: Sometimes, the people whose stories need telling can be hard to find.
sentences.zh: 有时候，那些其故事需要被讲述的人很难找到。

sentences.en: Seung helped us to bridge that gap. For more HIDDEN BRAIN, you can follow us on Facebook and Twitter.
sentences.zh: Seung 帮我们跨越了这道鸿沟。想要收听更多 HIDDEN BRAIN，您可以在 Facebook 和 Twitter 上关注我们。

sentences.en: If you like this episode, please remember to share it with a friend.
sentences.zh: 如果您喜欢本期节目，请记得分享给朋友。

sentences.en: We're always looking for new people to discover HIDDEN BRAIN.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在寻找发现 HIDDEN BRAIN 的新听众。

sentences.zh: 下周，我们将继续我们的“You 2.0”系列节目，探讨置身户外对健康的益处。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam, and this is NPR.
sentences.zh: 我是 Shankar Vedantam，这里是 NPR。
